text: He put an iron spike on top of his roof and told the whole town, when the next storm comes, stay away from the church.
The whole square burst out laughing.
You see, the church had the tallest bell tower for a hundred miles, and everybody knew church bells chased lightning away.
So every time thunder rolled, the bell ringers climbed the tower and rang as hard as they could.
The priest called his spike an insult to heaven, and the kids threw rocks at it.
Weeks later, a storm rolled in, and a bolt of lightning hit the spike. But nothing happened. Not even a scorch mark.
Ooh, your toothpick caught a spark! Very scary.
Then, one night, the biggest storm in years rolled in. The bells started ringing. The sky flashed white.
He ran to the church, screaming for everyone to get out.
Hey, it's the spike guy! Scared of a little rain?
The ringers laughed and kept on pulling.
The next morning, a sixth of the city was gone.
Under that bell tower, the government had hidden ninety tons of gunpowder.
The tower was the tallest thing in town, so the lightning hit it, tore down through the stone, and found the powder.
His spike gave the lightning a metal road straight into the ground. The church gave it a road straight into the powder.
